metrics.description: Total monetary value of goods or services sold before any deductions

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Revenue is a monetary value, not a countable entity

metrics.additivityNote: Revenue can be safely summed across all dimensions

confusionPairs.distinction: Revenue is total sales; profit is revenue minus cost/expenses

metrics.aiHint: When user says 'sales' they almost always mean revenue, not order count

metrics.description: Revenue minus cost of goods sold and/or operating expenses
metrics.additivityNote: Profit can be summed across all dimensions

confusionPairs.distinction: Profit accounts for costs; revenue does not
Profit is an absolute value; margin is a percentage

metrics.aiHint: If the dataset has revenue and cost but no profit column, it can be derived

metrics.description: Total cost of goods sold or cost of service delivery
metrics.additivityNote: Cost can be summed across all dimensions

confusionPairs.distinction: Cost is what the business pays; price is what the customer pays

metrics.aiHint: COGS specifically refers to cost of goods sold

metrics.description: Number of units sold, ordered, or produced
metrics.additivityNote: Quantity is fully additive

confusionPairs.distinction: Quantity is units per order; order count is number of orders

metrics.aiHint: Quantity typically appears at line-item grain, not order grain

metrics.description: Monetary value per unit of a product or service

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Summing prices across rows is almost always meaningless — use revenue instead

metrics.additivityNote: Price is per-unit and should NEVER be summed across rows

confusionPairs.distinction: Price is per-unit; revenue is price × quantity
Price is customer-facing; cost is business-facing

metrics.aiHint: CRITICAL: Never SUM price across rows. If user asks 'total price' they mean revenue.

metrics.description: Profit as a percentage of revenue: (Revenue - Cost) / Revenue × 100

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Margins are percentages — summing them is mathematically incorrect. Use weighted average.

metrics.additivityNote: Margin must be recalculated at each aggregation level, never summed

confusionPairs.distinction: Margin is a percentage; profit is an absolute dollar amount

metrics.aiHint: If user asks for 'margin' and it's not a column, derive from revenue and cost

metrics.description: Average revenue per order: Total Revenue / Number of Orders

aggregation.forbiddenReason: AOV is a per-order metric — summing it across orders is meaningless

metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated as SUM(revenue) / COUNT(DISTINCT orders) at each level

derivedFrom.formulaDescription: AOV = Total Revenue ÷ Number of Unique Orders

confusionPairs.distinction: AOV is revenue per order (may contain multiple items); price is per unit

metrics.aiHint: AOV is almost never stored as a column — it must be derived from revenue and order_id

metrics.description: Number of unique orders or transactions
metrics.additivityNote: Can be summed if pre-aggregated; use COUNT(DISTINCT) on raw data

confusionPairs.distinction: Order count is number of orders; quantity is number of items

metrics.aiHint: When counting orders, always use COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) not COUNT(*)

metrics.description: Number of unique customers

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Customer count must use COUNT(DISTINCT) — summing or averaging IDs is meaningless

metrics.additivityNote: Cannot be summed across time (same customer appears in multiple periods)

confusionPairs.distinction: One customer can place multiple orders

metrics.aiHint: Always COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id), never COUNT(*) or SUM

metrics.description: Price reduction applied to an order or product
metrics.additivityNote: Discount amounts are additive; discount rates are not

confusionPairs.distinction: Discount is absolute ($); discount rate is relative (%)

metrics.aiHint: Check if discount is stored as absolute value or percentage — this changes aggregation

metrics.description: Customer or employee satisfaction rating, typically on a 1-5 or 1-10 scale

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Summing satisfaction scores is meaningless — use average

metrics.additivityNote: Satisfaction is a rating — must be averaged, never summed

confusionPairs.distinction: Satisfaction is typically 1-5; NPS is -100 to +100

metrics.aiHint: If user asks 'total satisfaction' they mean average, not sum

metrics.description: Percentage of customers who stopped using the service in a period

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Churn rate is a percentage — summing it is meaningless

metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated at each aggregation level

derivedFrom.formulaDescription: Churn Rate = Churned Customers ÷ Total Customers × 100

confusionPairs.distinction: Churn = 1 - Retention

metrics.aiHint: Churn and retention are complements — always clarify which one the user wants

metrics.description: Percentage of visitors/leads that completed a desired action

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Conversion rate is a ratio — cannot be summed

metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated as conversions/visitors at each level
metrics.aiHint: If no conversion_rate column exists, try to derive from two count columns

metrics.description: Predictable monthly revenue from subscriptions
metrics.additivityNote: Additive across customers but NOT across time (it's a point-in-time snapshot)

confusionPairs.distinction: MRR counts only recurring subscription revenue, not one-time fees

metrics.aiHint: MRR is semi-additive — summing across months double-counts

metrics.description: Duration between admission and discharge in days
metrics.additivityNote: Can be summed for total patient-days, but average is more common

derivedFrom.formulaDescription: LOS = Discharge Date − Admission Date (in days)

metrics.aiHint: LOS is almost always derived from two date columns, not stored directly

metrics.description: Percentage of patients readmitted within a specified window (typically 30 days)
metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated per aggregation level
metrics.aiHint: Standard clinical definition is readmission within 30 days of discharge

metrics.description: Number of active employees (headcount)

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Employee IDs should be counted, not summed or averaged

metrics.additivityNote: Point-in-time metric — cannot sum across periods

confusionPairs.distinction: Headcount counts people; FTE adjusts for part-time

metrics.aiHint: Use COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) — some employees appear in multiple records

metrics.description: Employee compensation amount (annual or monthly)
metrics.additivityNote: Can sum for total payroll; avg for typical compensation

confusionPairs.distinction: Salary is base pay; total comp includes bonuses, equity, benefits

metrics.aiHint: When user asks 'average salary' they mean average per employee, not per department

metrics.description: Percentage of employees who left the organization in a period
metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated at each aggregation level

confusionPairs.distinction: Turnover is for employees; churn is for customers

metrics.aiHint: In HR context, 'churn' typically means employee turnover, not customer churn

metrics.description: Duration of employment in years or months

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Summing tenure across employees is meaningless

metrics.additivityNote: Tenure must be averaged per group, never summed
metrics.aiHint: Usually derived from hire_date, not stored as a column

metrics.description: Cost of delivering goods to the customer
metrics.additivityNote: Shipping costs can be summed across all dimensions

confusionPairs.distinction: Shipping cost is delivery-specific; cost (COGS) is product-specific

metrics.aiHint: Shipping cost is distinct from COGS — don't combine them unless asked for total cost

metrics.description: Percentage of orders or items returned by customers

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Return rate is a percentage — cannot be summed

metrics.additivityNote: Must be recalculated as returns/orders at each level

derivedFrom.formulaDescription: Return Rate = Returned Orders ÷ Total Orders × 100

metrics.aiHint: High return rates often indicate product quality or description issues

metrics.description: Number of unique patients

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Patient IDs should be counted, not summed

metrics.additivityNote: Same patient can appear across departments/periods

confusionPairs.distinction: One patient can have multiple encounters

metrics.aiHint: Use COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) — patients may have multiple encounters

metrics.description: Age of a person in years

aggregation.forbiddenReason: Summing ages is meaningless — use average

metrics.additivityNote: Age is a per-entity attribute, never summed
metrics.aiHint: If user asks 'total age' they almost certainly mean 'average age'

metrics.description: Physical weight measurement (kg or lbs)
metrics.additivityNote: Weight can be summed for total weight (e.g., shipment weight)
metrics.aiHint: In healthcare context, weight should be averaged per patient, not summed

concepts.description: Overall business or entity performance — maps to a bundle of KPIs
How much profit or margin the business generates
Rate of increase in key metrics over time
How efficiently resources are being used
Clinical quality and patient result metrics
